# Summarize Video

- Route: `/tools/summarize-video`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `summarize-video`

## Summary

Get a written summary of a lecture, meeting or tutorial, with chapters you can click, topics and on-screen text, made on our own GPU servers. (AI tools)

## Details

Nobody wants to re-watch an hour of meeting or lecture to find the five minutes that mattered. Media Manipulator watches and listens for you: it transcribes the speech with Whisper, looks at frames chosen where the picture changes with a vision model, and writes a summary from both, all on a GPU server we operate. The result is a short document: a title, a few sentences, chapters with start and end times, the topics, and the text that appeared on screen. Click a chapter to jump to that moment in your video, copy the whole thing as Markdown, or download it as Markdown or JSON. Summaries need a free account.
### What it does
- Writes a title and a three-to-six-sentence summary of the whole video.
- Splits the video into chapters with start and end times; clicking one jumps the player to that moment.
- Lists the topics and the text that appears on screen, with the time it first appears.
- Describes the picture and the speech, and notes what it could not do (for example, no speech).
- Writes the summary in the language you pick, or in the language that is spoken.
### How to use it
1. Sign in: A free account is enough.
2. Upload: A video, or an audio file.
3. Summarize: Speech and frames are analysed on our GPU server.
4. Read: Click chapters, copy Markdown, download .md or .json.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v, flv, wmv, mp3, wav, m4a
- Output: md, json
- Counts as one AI job; failed jobs are not counted.
- Length up to your plan's video duration limit.
### Technical details
- Speech is transcribed with Whisper; frames are picked at scene changes, up to your plan's frame budget (24 on Free, 48 on Premium, 96 on Pro), and described in batches by a vision model.
- A language model writes the summary from the transcript and the frame notes. Pro accounts can ask for a deeper summary from a larger model when it is available.
- A summary counts as one AI job from your daily allowance; a failed or refused job is not counted.
- The transcript is machine-generated, so names and numbers can be wrong. The summary says so in its notes.
### Use cases
- Meeting recap: Decisions and topics, with times to check the details.
- Lecture notes: Chapters per section and the slide text, to study from.
- Tutorial outline: The steps as chapters, so you can jump to the one you need.
- Interview overview: What was discussed, and where.
### FAQ
Q: Do I need an account?
A: Yes, a free account. Summaries run several AI models on our GPU server, so they are limited to signed-in users.
Q: What do I get?
A: A title, a short summary, chapters with start and end times, topics, on-screen text with times, a description of the picture and the speech, and notes about anything it could not do.
Q: Can I choose the language of the summary?
A: Yes. Pick one of the site's 18 languages, or "same as the speech" to write it in the spoken language.
Q: What if the video has no speech?
A: The summary is written from the picture alone and says so in its notes. A file with neither picture nor sound is refused and not counted.
Q: Is my video sent to a third party?
A: No. Every model runs on a GPU server we operate.
Q: Does this count against my allowance?
A: Yes, as one AI job. Failed jobs are not counted.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Use when someone wants the gist of a lecture, meeting or tutorial video without watching it: a title, a short summary, clickable chapters with times, topics and the on-screen text. Typical asks: "summarize this video", "make chapters for my recording".
When to send them elsewhere: For the full word-for-word text use Transcribe Video (transcribe-video). If the source is audio only, such as a podcast, use Summarize Audio (summarize-audio). For subtitle files use SRT Generator (srt-generator).
Related tools: summarize-audio (the same for audio recordings); transcribe-video (full transcript instead of a summary); transcribe-audio (full transcript of audio); srt-generator (subtitle file for the video)
